We compared the eﬀect strength of limited time perspective on
distortion for the two studies that aimed at examining the main eﬀect
and thereby included a single distortion score (study 1 and study 3). In
study 1, Cohen’s d reached 0.39 and power reached 0.79, which sug-
gests a moderate eﬀect. In study 3, the eﬀect was conﬁrmed with a
similar Cohen’s d at 0.38. Yet, power only reached 0.65, due to study 3’s
smaller sample size. To further complete the analysis of the reliability of
the eﬀect, we also conducted a single paper meta-analysis (SPM;
McShane & Böckenholt, 2017). We analyzed the diﬀerence between the
control condition and the limited FTP condition in study 1 and study 3
(one factor, two levels, two studies, see Table 2). The SPM yielded an
overall contrast eﬀect of 0.49 units of distortion (SE = 0.16; 95% CI:
0.18−0.80). The conﬁdence interval does not include zero, indicating
that the impact of limited time perspective on distortion is sizable and
reliable.
